title: Data Poisoning Attacks Can Systematically Destabilize Data-Driven Control Synthesis
summary: Data-driven control has emerged as a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers directly from data, bypassing explicit model identification. However, this reliance on data introduces new and largely unexplored vulnerabilities. In this paper, we show that an attacker can systematically poison the data used for control synthesis, causing any linear state-feedback controller synthesized by the planner to destabilize the physical system.
